en.intro: Arjuna stops arguing and tells Krishna what he has learned. Listen to the one name he uses for him.
en.notice: Arjuna calls him Kamalapatraksha, lotus-eyed. This name points to the eyes. Arjuna has heard about the imperishable majesty, and is ready to see it.
en.next: He asks to see the divine form, saying everything Krishna has said is true.
en.meaning: O lotus-eyed one, I have heard from You in detail about the arising and passing away of all beings, and also about Your imperishable majesty.

hi.intro: अर्जुन अब तर्क नहीं कर रहे, वे कृष्ण को बता रहे हैं कि उन्होंने क्या सुना है। सुनिए, वे उन्हें क्या नाम देते हैं।
hi.meaning: हे कमलनयन, मैंने आपसे विस्तारपूर्वक सम्पूर्ण प्राणियों की उत्पत्ति और प्रलय के बारे में सुना है और आपका अविनाशी माहात्म्य भी सुना है।
hi.notice: अर्जुन उन्हें कमलपत्राक्ष कहते हैं, यानी कमल जैसी आँखों वाले। यह नाम आँखों की ओर इशारा करता है। अर्जुन ने अविनाशी माहात्म्य सुना है, और अब उसे देखने के लिए तैयार हैं।
hi.next: वे कहते हैं कि आपने अपने बारे में जो कुछ भी कहा है वह सत्य है, फिर भी वे आपका दिव्य रूप देखना चाहते हैं।

en.intro: Arjuna stops arguing and tells Krishna what he has learned. Listen to the one name he uses for him.
en.body: O lotus-eyed one, I have heard from You in detail about the arising and passing away of all beings, and also about Your imperishable majesty. Arjuna calls him Kamalapatraksha, lotus-eyed. This name points to the eyes. Arjuna has heard about the imperishable majesty, and is ready to see it. He asks to see the divine form, saying everything Krishna has said is true.

issues: unsupported: "He goes on to say that he wishes to see the divine form with his own eyes." (The Hindi 'next' claims Arjuna says he wishes to see the divine form with his own eyes (अपनी आँखों से देखना चाहते हैं). However, this is from the English 'next', which describes verse 3. The Hindi 'next' is just a translation of the English 'next', but the English 'next' itself is not a correct description of verse 3. The actual next verse (verse 3) is 'O Supreme Person, everything you have said about yourself is true. Yet I wish to see your divine form.' The phrase 'with his own eyes' (अपनी आँखों से) is an unsupported addition to the text of verse 3.)

unsupported: "This name points to the eyes, and in the next breath he says he has heard about the imperishable majesty, setting up the vision of the eyes that will see it." (The Hindi 'notice' claims that the name 'Kamalapatraksha' points to the eyes, and that in the 'next breath' Arjuna says he has heard about the imperishable majesty, setting up the vision of the eyes that will see it. The phrase 'in the next breath' (अगले ही पल) is an unsupported narrative detail not found in the source text.)
